prose:outro-stochastic-mechanics:
Chapter close — Stochastic mechanics.

This closes the stochastic-mechanics chapter. The Markov closure map, the classical-limit functor and its adelic arithmetic consequences, the \Phi_q / A_J machinery, the Lusztig canonical basis at q = 1, and the reverse limit q \to \infty assemble the Markov-trace stochastic dynamics on the aether.

The next chapter (Information-Theoretic Perspectives) recasts this Reeb-driven Markov dynamics in informational terms: Planck-scale operations, information speed c_q, reversible braid computation, q-statistical mechanics, and computational horizons.
sec:info-theory-intro:
The categorical framework of the QOU determines the information-theoretic structure of the universe. This chapter derives the Planck scale, the speed of light, mass--energy equivalence, the gravitational constant, and the operational entropy from the aether parameter q and the Reeb derivation. One then develops the computational consequences: a categorical criterion for P \neq NP, a Turing-complete Skein machine, and a conformal cyclic cosmology where aeon boundaries are categorical horizons.

Emergent gravity arises from the information geometry of the Frobenius--Hopf state space. The Planck time equals one Reeb operation. The speed of light c_q = 1/(q-1) and the reduced Planck constant \hbar_q = (q-1)/q follow strictly from the aether parameter.

The computational and cosmological implications include the P-bandwidth bound, statistical mechanics on the brane tower, and the horizon functor that implements Penrose's conformal cyclic cosmology within the QOU framework.
sec:emergent-gravity-info:
One derives the gravitational constant G_q from the q-Yang--Mills--Levi action (q-YM-Levi). The coupling is determined by the in-progress braid content of a Planck cell. These are sections of the jet tower A_0 \hookrightarrow A_1 \hookrightarrow \cdots that remain partially evaluated and not yet resolved to observable knots.

The central formula is:

  G_q = \frac{c_q^3 \hbar_q}{S_{\mathrm{cell}}}.

Here S_{\mathrm{cell}} measures the total information content per fibre, counting all in-progress braids. To maintain self-consistency with Planck units, the cell entropy must evaluate to S_{\mathrm{cell}} = (q-1)^2/q^3 \approx 0.009 q-bits. This represents 1.0\% of the single-operation entropy \eta_q \approx 0.892. The small ratio reflects the sparsity of partially-evaluated braids in the near-classical regime.

Gravity is weak because most braiding at a typical fibre is already resolved. Fully resolved braids contribute to T^{(q)} as matter. Only the unresolved, in-progress tails establish the gravitational coupling.
sec:planck-info-unit: The local per-step Reeb share \hbar_q(p) = 1 - q(p)^{-1} sets the minimal quantisable grain of an information unit at a point p \in M. An elementary information unit at p scales with the aether parameter as \hbar_q(p) --- the fraction of one Reeb circuit traversed per elementary connection step, distinct from the unit-normalised full circuit \hbar_q \cdot t_P = 1.
sec:info-time-computation-preamble: This section establishes the framework for time and computation. The following blocks trace the construction from time-info onward.
sec:time-info:
Time in the QOU is not an external parameter. It is the dynamics. The fundamental time variable is information-theoretic time \mathcal{T}. This measures the cumulative count of Reeb operations (iterations of the Julia set map f_q(z) = z^2 + c(q) on the exceptional divisor). Each operation represents one braiding evaluation, one jet prolongation, and one tick of the braiding-induced ordering \prec_c on the Hecke basis.

The continuous time coordinate t of the Reeb flow \phi_t^q emerges from \mathcal{T} via statistical mechanical coarse-graining: t = \hbar_q \mathcal{T}. The quantum Planck constant \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} plays the role of Boltzmann's constant. At the Big Bang (q \to \infty, \hbar_q \to 1), t = \mathcal{T} and time is a natural number. Each tick is individually meaningful. At the local aether parameter (q = q_0, \hbar_q \approx 0.1), approximately 10 discrete operations compose each Planck unit. The continuous approximation carries an O(\hbar_q) \approx 10\% error. At the classical limit (q \to 1, \hbar_q \to 0), infinitely many operations per unit make time smooth.

This section defines the Planck time. It counts the Reeb operations per Planck unit as a function of q. It defines information-theoretic time. Finally, it constructs the statistical mechanical bridge from discrete computation to continuous flow.
def:planck-time:
Definition Planck Time. Let q \in k^\times \setminus \{1\} denote the aether parameter (aether parameter). Let \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} denote the quantum Planck constant (quantum Planck constant). One defines the Planck time as

  t_P(q)  :=  \frac{1}{\hbar_q}
  =  \frac{q}{q - 1}.

This rational function of q is defined over any field k where q \neq 1.
rem:planck-time-interpretation:
Remark Planck time: Reeb-circuit reading, regimes, field realisations, and the Planck length. Interpretation. One Planck time equals the period of a single full circuit of the q-Reeb flow (q-Reeb flow). One measures this in discrete f_q-iterations on the exceptional divisor. One circuit comprises t_P(q) iterations of f_q(z) = z^2 + c(q). At the deep-quantum limit (t_P = 1), one iteration completes one circuit. At the physical aether value q = q_0 (local aether q), roughly 10 iterations compose one circuit. The reciprocal \hbar_q = 1/t_P represents the angular velocity: the fraction of a full circuit completed per f_q-iteration.

Regime table.

Regime q \hbar_q t_P Interpretation
Deep-quantum q \to \infty \to 1 \to 1 One f_q-step per circuit; fully discrete
Physical q = q_0 0.0988 \approx 10.1 \sim 10 f_q-steps per Reeb circuit
Classical q \to 1 \to 0 \to \infty Infinitely many steps; continuous flow

Field realisations.

  • Over \mathbb{F}_\pp: t_P = q/(q-1) \in \mathbb{F}_\pp for q \in \mathbb{F}_\pp^\times \setminus \{1\}. One Planck step evaluates f_q(z) = z^2 + c(q) once.
  • Over \mathbb{Q}_\pp: The valuation v_\pp(t_P) = v_\pp(q) - v_\pp(q-1) encodes the \pp-adic proximity of q to the classical limit.
  • Over \mathbb{C}: This reproduces the angular period T = 2\pi/\hbar_q, up to the conventional factor 2\pi.

Planck length. After one Planck time of Reeb flow, the angular displacement is

  \ell_P(q) =  \hbar_q \cdot t_P =  1

This identity holds over any field. The Planck length equals 1. The parameter q varies only the number of discrete operations t_P(q) composing that unit displacement.
def:information-theoretic-time:
Definition Information-Theoretic Time. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with braiding-induced ordering \prec_c (ordering–jet compatibility). Let f_q(z) = z^2 + c(q) be the Julia set iteration on the exceptional divisor.

The information-theoretic time at aether parameter q is the cumulative Reeb operation count:

  \mathcal{T}(q)  :=  \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} 1
  =  N

where N is the total number of iterations of f_q applied since a reference configuration \mathcal{S}_0. Each iteration advances the admissible ordering by one step. The count \mathcal{T} determines the position in the braiding-induced ordering \prec_c propagated through the jet tower.
prop:reeb-operations-per-planck:
Proposition Discrete iterations per Reeb circuit. Let q \in k^\times \setminus \{1\}. Let t_P(q) = q/(q-1) be the Planck time (Planck time). The number of discrete f_q-iterations (evaluations of f_q(z) = z^2 + c(q) on the exceptional divisor) comprising one Reeb circuit is

  n_R(q) =  t_P(q) =  \frac{q}{q - 1} =  \frac{1}{\hbar_q}.

Each iteration executes one braiding evaluation (a single R-matrix application) and one jet prolongation step. Together, these advance the phase by exactly the fraction \hbar_q of a full circuit.
prf:reeb-operations-per-planck:
Proof Proof of reeb operations per planck. The Reeb time coordinate is defined as t = \hbar_q \cdot \mathcal{T} (information-theoretic time). Consequently, each discrete f_q-iteration (an increment of \mathcal{T} by 1) corresponds to a continuous time duration of \hbar_q. The number of iterations composing one full Reeb circuit (continuous duration 1) is therefore exactly 1/\hbar_q = t_P(q). \square

Regime values.

q n_R Interpretation
\to \infty \to 1 Deep-quantum: one iteration per circuit, fully discrete
q_0 \approx 10.1 The observed universe (local aether q): \sim 10 iterations per circuit
2 2 Two iterations per circuit
1.01 101 Near-classical: \sim 100 iterations per circuit
\to 1 \to \infty Classical limit: infinitely many, continuous Reeb flow

Information rate. The information processed per Planck unit is

  I_P(q) =  n_R(q) \cdot \eta_q.

Here \eta_q = (2q-1)/q^3 is the operational entropy. This parameter quantifies the information generated per f_q-iteration, dictated strictly by the gravitational self-consistency condition.

In the deep-quantum regime (q \to \infty), n_R \to 1 and \eta_q \to 0. The dynamics simplify entirely, yielding I_P \to 0. At the classical limit (q \to 1), \eta_q \to 1 nat per step. At q = q_0, I_P \approx 10.1 \times 0.892 \approx 9.0 q-bits per Planck time.
rem:reeb-operations-per-planck-physical:
Remark Physical meaning of the Reeb operation count at q = q_0. At the local aether parameter q_0 (local aether q), approximately 10 iterations of the Julia set dynamics f_q occur within each Planck time. Each iteration:

  1. Advances the phase of the Reeb vector by \hbar_q \approx 0.099 of a full circuit.
  2. Applies the q-connection \nabla_q once, correlating adjacent fibers.
  3. Evaluates one R-matrix, resolving one braiding crossing on the exceptional divisor.

The link-length resolution within the exceptional divisor grows with each operation. After n steps, the divisor resolves knots up to crossing number n. Within a single Planck time at q = q_0, the exceptional divisor completes \sim 10 braiding evaluations. This provides ample capacity to resolve the full electron-positron sector (c = 3).
rem:information-theoretic-time-propertie:
Remark Reeb time coordinate, three regimes, and the arrow of time. The information-theoretic time \mathcal{T}(q) (information-theoretic time) rescales to the continuous Reeb time coordinate. It passes through three regimes—discrete, statistical, and continuous—acting as a statistical-mechanical coarse-graining.

Reeb time coordinate. The continuous time coordinate t of the q-Reeb flow (q-Reeb flow) is the rescaled operation count:

  t =  \frac{\mathcal{T}}{t_P(q)}
  =  \hbar_q \cdot \mathcal{T}

where t_P(q) = q/(q-1) is the Planck time (Planck time). The denominator t_P(q) is the number of discrete f_q iterations per Reeb circuit (iterations per Reeb circuit). Dividing by it converts the integer step count \mathcal{T} into a continuous flow parameter.

Three regimes.

  1. Discrete regime (q \to \infty, deep-quantum). t_P \to 1, so t = \mathcal{T}. The Reeb time coordinate equals the integer step count. Each tick represents one braiding, one jet prolongation, or one link resolved in the exceptional divisor. There is no sub-step structure and no averaging. Time is a natural number.

  2. Statistical regime (q = q_0 (local aether q), the observed universe). t_P \approx 10. Approximately 10 Reeb operations compose each Planck unit. Individual operations are not separately resolvable at the Planck scale. One observes their aggregate: the statistical average of \sim 10 braiding evaluations. The Reeb flow parameter t becomes a coarse-grained time that smooths over discrete steps, just as thermodynamic quantities smooth over microscopic states.

  3. Continuous regime (q \to 1, classical limit). t_P \to \infty. Infinitely many operations occur per unit. The discrete structure vanishes. The parameter t is a smooth real variable and the Reeb flow \phi_t^q is a genuine one-parameter group of diffeomorphisms. Time is \mathbb{R}-valued.

The thermodynamic bridge. The passage from regime 1 to regime 3 is the statistical mechanical coarse-graining of time. For any smooth observable g on the Reeb flow, the discrete time-average over one circuit (t_P steps) is a Riemann sum:

  \frac{1}{t_P} \sum_{n=0}^{t_P - 1} g\!\left(\frac{n}{t_P}\right)
  \xrightarrow{t_P \to \infty}
  \int_0^1 g(s)ds.

The left side is the average of g over t_P discrete Reeb operations. The right side is the continuous-flow time-average. They agree to O(1/t_P) = O(\hbar_q). The error vanishes precisely as the quantum Planck constant goes to zero.

At q = q_0 (local aether q), one has t_P \approx 10. The Riemann approximation has O(1/10) \approx 10\% relative error. This marks the scale where discreteness is marginally detectable, aligning with quantum-gravitational corrections as O(\hbar_q) effects.
rem:information-theoretic-time-julia-mic:
Remark Julia-set iteration as the microscopic theory of time. One grounds the information-theoretic time (information-theoretic time) in a microscopic dynamical theory: the Julia-set iteration f_q. The thermodynamic limit of this iteration yields the continuous Reeb flow.

Julia set dynamics as the microscopic theory. One interprets the iteration f_q(z) = z^2 + c(q) on the exceptional divisor as the microscopic dynamics of time. Each iterate f_q^{\circ n}(z_0) constitutes one microstate of the temporal evolution. The continuous Reeb flow \phi_t^q emerges as the macroscopic limit, obtained by averaging over t_P(q) microscopic iterates per unit.

The Julia set J(f_q) is the boundary separating escaping and bounded orbits. Its Hausdorff dimension d_H(q) measures the complexity of the time evolution at parameter q. A higher d_H indicates that the microscopic dynamics explores more phase space per operation, so macroscopic time carries more information per unit.
rem:information-theoretic-time-arrow:
Remark The arrow of time inherited from the braiding order. The information-theoretic time inherits its direction from the braiding order \prec_c. The arrow of time is not re-derived in the continuous limit.

Consistency with the arrow of time. The braiding-induced ordering \prec_c on the Hecke basis (ordering–jet compatibility) propagates through the jet tower. This defines forward and backward time at every brane level. One defines the information-theoretic time \mathcal{T} as the counting measure on this well-ordering: \mathcal{T}(a) < \mathcal{T}(b) iff a \prec_c b. The rescaling t = \hbar_q \mathcal{T} preserves the order, ensuring the Reeb time coordinate inherits the same arrow.
rem:statistical-mechanical-time:
Remark Statistical mechanical emergence of continuous time. The information-theoretic time acts as a strict counting measure on discrete Reeb operations. The passage to a smooth time coordinate entails a statistical coarse-graining, structurally analogous to the emergence of thermodynamic quantities from microscopic dynamics.

The analogy. See Table.

The mechanism of passing from a Riemann sum to an integral drives both the emergence of thermodynamic equilibrium from molecular collisions and the emergence of continuous time from discrete Reeb operations.

Crossover at \sim 10 operations. At q = q_0 (local aether q), one has t_P \approx 10.1 (iterations per Reeb circuit). The central limit theorem applies to sums of \sim 10 independent operations. Statistical fluctuations scale as O(1/\sqrt{10}) \approx 30\%. This large variance implies individual discrete steps are not fully smoothed. Quantum-gravitational discreteness reliably produces O(\hbar_q) \approx 10\% corrections to the continuous Reeb flow.

Conversely, at q = 1.01 (t_P \approx 101), fluctuations drop to O(1/\sqrt{101}) \approx 10\%. At q = 1.001, they fall to \sim 3\% and time effectively smooths.

Exceptional divisor dynamics at each scale. At the Big Bang (t_P = 1), each Planck unit captures exactly one braiding evaluation on the exceptional divisor. The link-length resolution increases by precisely one crossing per tick. Dynamics remain fully resolved. The Julia set iteration f_q executes once.

At q = q_0 (t_P \approx 10), each Planck unit executes \sim 10 braiding evaluations. The exceptional divisor undergoes \sim 10 iterations of f_q. The aggregate effect resolving 10 crossings is fully observable. However, the intermediate states cannot be individually resolved at the Planck scale.

At the classical limit (t_P \to \infty), infinitely many iterations fill each unit. The Julia set dynamics degenerates into continuous Reeb flow. The orbit structure flattens into the smooth invariant measure \mu_J.

Connection to jet prolongation. Each Reeb operation executes exactly one jet prolongation. The \sim 10 jet prolongations occurring within a single Planck time generate a statistical jet, which averages the intermediate polynomial orders. The continuous limit (q \to 1) recovers the analytic germ J^\infty E. The smooth Taylor series arises as the thermodynamic limit of the discrete jet tower.

sec:big-bang-info:
At \mathcal{T} = 0, no Reeb operation has occurred. The initial state specifies fiber data without horizontal transport. No information has propagated. Position is known exactly; momentum is entirely undetermined.

At \mathcal{T} = 1, the first iteration of f_q connects neighboring fibers. The q-connection \nabla_q acts once. Over \mathbb{F}_\pp, this reduces to z_1 = z_0^2 + c(q). The Heisenberg commutator [\hat{X}, \hat{P}]_q = J\hbar_q is near-maximal.

Because t_P \to 1 at the Big Bang, the information-theoretic time \mathcal{T} and the Reeb time coordinate t coincide: t = \hbar_q \mathcal{T} \approx \mathcal{T}. There is no coarse-graining. One resolves each braiding on the exceptional divisor individually. The particle spectrum unfolds step by step through the jet prolongation tower.
sec:planck-computation:
The number of Reeb operations per Planck unit, n_R(q) = q/(q-1) (Reeb operations per Planck unit), determines the computational capacity of a Planck-length region.

Each operation evaluates f_q(z) = z^2 + c(q). It resolves one crossing in the braid representation of the local link structure. The total computational work per Planck unit equals n_R(q) polynomial evaluations.

At q = q_0, a Planck-length region performs roughly 10 polynomial evaluations per Planck time. This defines the microscopic computational rate of the universe at the observed scale. It represents the clock speed of the exceptional divisor dynamics, which coarse-grains into the smooth Reeb flow.
rem:computational-spacetime-observer:
Remark Computational spacetime and the observer. Time relative to the observer. In the QOU formalism, time is not an absolute background parameter but is relative to the observer. The "time" experienced by an observer is the computational time required to evaluate the state space leading to or following from that point. This discrete sequence of Planck operations acts as the metric of temporal distance; the underlying definition is information-theoretic time.

Categorical dynamics

At the Planck length, geometric coordinates give way to a purely categorical framing of the observer and the time step. Let the observable universe M be an object in a category \mathbf{C} with a terminal object \mathrm{pt}.

Point morphisms and particles. A geometric "point" is a morphism p : \mathrm{pt} \to M. A particle is not a point but a section over points: a morphism s : M \to E into a bundle E \to M whose composition with the projection is the identity. The state of the particle at a point is the composition of p with s.

Functorial evolution. Dynamical evolution is modeled as an endofunctor on the category, or equivalently as an endomorphism \mathrm{TimeStep} : M \to M. The "flowed" state of a point under one Planck time step is the composition

  p \;\mapsto\; p \circ \mathrm{TimeStep} .

The unification dictionary

The framework treats time-step evolution as a generic endofunctor. One expects — by analogy with the coherence theorems for braided monoidal categories — that a functorial time step preserving the QOU invariants is naturally isomorphic to the fundamental braiding action; this uniqueness is a heuristic identification here, not a proved statement. Under that identification, four conceptual domains would describe the same underlying mechanism of the discrete computational Planck step:

Conceptual domain Mechanism / object Evolution action
Category theory Point morphism p : \mathrm{pt} \to M Endofunctor F, flow p \circ F
Algebraic / knot theory State-space braiding R-matrix operator \check{R}, Markov trace
Conformal field theory Exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_p Vertex operator Y(a, z), OPE singularity
Information theory Computational spacetime Discrete Planck operation, evaluation step

Read this dictionary as a proposed correspondence: the computational time-step functor acting on point morphisms would be instantiated by the R-matrix operator on the state space, which in turn evaluates as a vertex-operator insertion on Bring's surface.

Bring's surface and the emergence of spacetime

The relationship between time, algebraic distance, and computational cost is carried by the first two coordinates of Bring's surface. Bring's surface has 2 complex dimensions; under the action of the natural involution these supply the 4 real dimensions interpreted as physical spacetime. The first two coordinates of Bring's surface map into the computational spacetime metric.

Relative distance as computational cost. On this reading, physical distance is relative computational time: the separation between two events is the number of discrete lattice applications of the R-matrix (dependent on the local aether parameter q) required to connect their state spaces. While this computational distance is relative to the observer, it remains consistent across observers: the algebraic consistency of the state space (the Yang--Baxter equations on the R-matrix) makes the computational distance agree across observers, so macroscopic symmetries such as Lorentz covariance would emerge as information-theoretic agreement. This recovery of Lorentz covariance is an interpretive expectation, not a derivation.

The aether parameter and the mass ratio

In the trace-based mass channel, particle masses are computed from the Markov trace of their respective topological knots,

  \mathfrak{m}(K) \;\approx\; \mathrm{tr}_M(K, q) \cdot \mathfrak{E}_0 ,

with \mathfrak{E}_0 the scaling energy. For the ratio between two flavor generations (the muon and the electron), the scaling energy cancels, leaving an algebraic relation

  \frac{\mathfrak{m}_\mu}{\mathfrak{m}_e} \;=\; \frac{\mathrm{tr}_M(K_\mu, q)}{\mathrm{tr}_M(K_e, q)} .

This identity suggests a physical reading of the aether parameter q: rather than a hidden background parameter, q is tied directly to the mass ratio itself. If q is a local field q(p) that evolves in response to local interactions (for example in regions of extreme electromagnetic field or gravity), then a topological deformation of the local geometry would manifest as a shift in the local mass ratio \mathfrak{m}_\mu(p)/\mathfrak{m}_e(p), and tracking the evolution of q(p) over the spacetime lattice would be observationally equivalent to tracking a drift of the flavor mass hierarchy. Both the local-field promotion of q and the resulting drift are speculative interpretations of the trace identity.
prop:reeb-coefficient-is-hbar-q:
Proposition The Reeb coefficient of D_\nabla is the quantum Planck constant: 1 - q^{-1} = (q-1)/q. The categorical Dirac operator splits its action into a gradient part and a contact part,

  D_\nabla \;=\; q^{-1}\,\nabla \;+\; \bigl(1 - q^{-1}\bigr)\,\iota_\xi \nabla ,

and its Reeb coefficient is the quantum Planck constant:

  \boxed{\;\; 1 - q^{-1} \;=\; \frac{q-1}{q} \;=\; \hbar_q. \;\;}

The identity is immediate --- both sides clear to q - 1 over q --- and that is the point. Two quantities introduced for unrelated reasons turn out to be one quantity. The coefficient of \iota_\xi\nabla was fixed by demanding that the Dirac operator weight the Reeb direction consistently with the q-connection; the quantum Planck constant was defined as the deformation gap (q-1)/q that measures how far the aether sits from the classical point q = 1. Neither definition mentions the other.

What the identification says

The quantum Planck constant is a weight, not a length. It is the share of a single application of D_\nabla that flows along the Reeb direction, and the complementary share q^{-1} flows along the gradient. The two are a convex pair, q^{-1} + (1 - q^{-1}) = 1, so the operator is a genuine mixture of the two directions at every q strictly between the classical and Big Bang limits.

Reading \hbar_q as a step cost rather than as a distance settles the relation to the Planck step. Since t_P = 1/\hbar_q counts Reeb operations per unit of time, the product \hbar_q \cdot t_P is the whole circuit, and the two symbols measure a fraction and its reciprocal rather than two competing scales.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs --- real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the aether parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here. At q_0 = 1.10997858275138080759 the Reeb share is \hbar_{q_0} = 0.09908171604425850784 and the gradient share is q_0^{-1} = 0.90091828395574149216, with t_P(q_0) = 10.09267945615024539110.
rem:connes-distance-not-reeb-step-count:
Remark d_{\mathrm{Connes}} is a minimal Reeb step count only in the q \to \infty limit. A spectral distance built from D_\nabla is often read as counting Reeb steps: the minimal number of applications of the flow needed to carry one state to another. The reading is available only in a limit, and the qualification belongs next to the identification of the Reeb coefficient rather than in a footnote to it.

The two coefficients of D_\nabla are a convex pair,

  q^{-1} \;+\; \bigl(1 - q^{-1}\bigr) \;=\; 1 ,

with q^{-1} weighting the gradient direction and \hbar_q = 1-q^{-1} the Reeb direction. A metric induced by D_\nabla therefore measures a mixture. It reduces to a pure Reeb step count exactly when the gradient share vanishes, that is as q \to \infty, where the operator becomes purely contact. At the opposite end, q = 1, the Reeb share vanishes and the operator is pure gradient --- the classical point, where there is no Reeb period at all.

At the aether parameter the mixture is lopsided in the wrong direction for the step-count reading. The gradient carries 90.09\,\% of the weight and the Reeb direction 9.908\,\%, so nine parts in ten of what the metric measures is not Reeb transport. Any identification of d_{\mathrm{Connes}} with a minimal step count at q_0 would therefore be off by an order of magnitude in its dominant term, and the gap is not a small correction to be absorbed.

Two obstructions to the spectral-distance programme are in play and they are independent. The mixing above says that even a well-defined distance is not the quantity one wanted. Separately, the degeneracy obstruction says the distance built from the Markov--Gram form is not well-defined at all until the radical is quotiented away. Repairing either leaves the other standing.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs --- real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the aether parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here. The percentages above are q_0^{-1} = 0.90091828395574149216 and \hbar_{q_0} = 0.09908171604425850784.
rem:planck-length-share-vs-total:
Remark \ell_P carries two meanings: the Reeb share \hbar_q and the normalised total \ell_P(q) \equiv 1. The symbol \ell_P appears twice in this chapter with two different referents, and read carelessly the two look like a disagreement by a factor of t_P \approx 10.1. They are not in disagreement. One is a share and the other is the total.

The share. At a point p of the brane, the Planck information unit sets the minimal quantisable grain of an information unit and scales it with \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}. What is being named is the fraction of one Reeb circuit traversed by a single application of the connection: the per-step share. The scaling carries \hbar_q as a weight: it is the Reeb coefficient of the categorical Dirac operator, which is what the Reeb coefficient identity establishes.

The total. After one Planck step, the displacement is

  \ell_P(q) \;=\; \hbar_q \cdot t_P \;=\; \bigl(1-q^{-1}\bigr)\cdot\frac{q}{q-1} \;=\; 1 .

What is being named here is the normalised total: one full Reeb circuit, an angular displacement carrying no length scale, set to unity so that the transcendental period 2\pi never enters and the construction survives over a finite field.

Why the two are consistent

The Planck time is defined as the reciprocal of the Reeb share, t_P = 1/\hbar_q, so the product of share and reciprocal is the circuit by construction. Writing \hbar_q for the share and \ell_P(q) = 1 for the circuit states that each step covers the fraction \hbar_q of a single unit-normalised Reeb period.

The notation register keeps one symbol per mathematical object by writing \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} = (q-1)/q directly for the per-step share across both information theory and brane fluid dynamics (where kinematic viscosity is \nu_q = \hbar_q / 2), while reserving \ell_P(q) = \hbar_q \cdot t_P = 1 for the normalised full circuit.
sec:golden-julia-dynamics-intro:
The Reeb flow on the exceptional divisor does not inherently require a discrete time step. Here, one discretizes it into Planck units to read off the symbolic dynamics on the Descartes elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q. The golden ratio \varphi appears twice: as a metric ratio at q_0 and as an algebraic root at q_{\mathrm{gold}} = 1/\varphi^2.

The remarks that follow establish this structure. Parallel transport of a golden-ratio parallelogram to q_{\mathrm{gold}} carries a fundamental domain of the chiral fiber along the q-connection. This demonstrates that the two occurrences of \varphi represent the same algebraic number viewed from opposite ends of the aether parameter space. The Julia set of the Reeb flow identifies the invariant set of the iterated Reeb map. One then defines the operational entropy of the Reeb dynamics to extract the metric entropy \eta_q = (2q-1)/q^3 via the Bowen--Ruelle thermodynamic formalism.

One Planck step of Reeb flow anchors the time variable at the Big Bang initial state \mathcal{S}_0. rem:jet-planck-encodability-vs-scatterin:

sec:speed-of-light-intro:
Having established the Reeb-flow operational entropy and the Planck step, one now extracts a velocity and a mass--energy law. The q-connection on the state bundle, operating at the aether parameter q_0, natively defines a Lieb--Robinson cone for information propagation. This causal cone forms the physical speed of light.

The speed of light emerges as the Lieb--Robinson velocity c_q = 1/(q-1). This bounds the maximum information bandwidth per Planck step. A rigorous mass--energy equivalence (E_{\mathfrak{H}} = \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{H}} \cdot c_q^2) follows immediately by evaluating the categorical trace of the crossing energy within the ribbon category. Mass \mathfrak{m} assumes a Gröbner–Shirshov interpretation: it quantifies the topological cost of threading a photon through a knot. Subsequently, the gravitational constant G_q aligns with Jacobson's entropy--area derivation via information geometry, and takes the closed q-rational form G_q = q^2/(q-1)^4, which is 1 in Planck units. The Hausdorff dimension d_H(q) = (2q-1)^2/q^3 directly governs the discrete recurrence, saturating the Margolus--Levitin bound. These parameters—c_q and the bandwidth budget \mathfrak{B}(q)—will strictly bound every Toffoli step.
